feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 1 (best, 114.4) had oval progress 0.47, max_error 0.061 to 0.066 m and oval steering oscillation 0.28. Iteration 5 moved the lead to 0.02 m and scored 91.8, with s-bend progress falling to 0.11 and oscillation falling to 0.24. That suggests a shorter lead loses look-ahead on bends, so this candidate tests a longer lead of 0.04 m. The Integrator kept the iteration-1 controller (kp 2.5, kd 0.30, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), so the only change in the race is the sensor row moving to y = 0.04 m. Integration point: the sensors now see the line about 1 cm earlier, so the controller reacts earlier and may overshoot if the lead is too long for the bend rate. Change the next design by what the race shows. If s-bend progress rises above 0.26 and oval progress holds at or above 0.47, with max_error at or below about 0.06 m, keep the longer lead and refine it toward 0.045 m or try mass 0.55 kg for damping. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 or line-loss events increase on the slalom, the longer lead is lagging, so return the sensors to y 0.03 m and try wheel_track 0.11 m for damping. If progress falls on both tracks with no gain in max_error, the lead optimum is near 0.03 m, so keep 0.03 m and move to the drivetrain levers.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress is above 0.26 and oval progress is at or above 0.47 with max_error at or below 0.06 m, keep sensor y at 0.04 m and set mass to 0.55 kg (from 0.6). Iteration 4 showed that a lighter body raises oscillation (0.33), so take only a small step.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 or slalom line_loss_events rise above the iteration-1 level of 0.3, return sensor y to 0.03 m and set wheel_track to 0.11 m (from 0.10). Iteration 0 with a 0.12 m track gave lower oval oscillation (0.085), so this trades some turn authority for damping.

If max_error does not fall below about 0.065 m and progress drops on both oval and s-bend, keep sensor y at 0.03 m and do not move the lead again. Iteration 5 (0.02 m) showed that shortening the lead hurts progress, and this test will show whether lengthening it helps.
